about: What each treasure needs inside its level, besides the level being open (tools/treasure_graph.py works that out from the game data).

needs: treasure -> where that need comes from, one of: "guide" (a guide says it), "game data" (a treasure's change of this level, LevelTreasureRequirements / OWSceneParams, matched to this chest), "heuristic (power-up map flash + lowest chest)" (a power-up flashes this level on the map and this is the lowest-colour chest not yet obtainable there), "verified in game by Taro". The value can also be {"by": one of those, "note": "free text"}. A power-up treasure (LEAD_OVERALLS_T ... SUPER_GRAB_GLOVES_T) means that power-up level or higher.

Recording a check made in the game: set each need that was confirmed to {"by": "verified in game by Taro", "note": "..."}, delete the needs that turned out not to be needed (and add any that were missing), then add "verified": {"by": "verified in game by Taro", "note": "..."} to the treasure: that takes it off the review list. Then run python3 tools/treasure_graph.py to rewrite the page and the review list.
check: what to try in the game, shown on the review list.
status: guide = a guide says so and the game data agrees; data = from the game data (and the heuristic) alone; uncertain = sources missing, conflicting or not conclusive.
The guides were read through web search results: the sites couldn't be opened from where this was written. Check the page before relying on a detail.
